Do you understand the acid-base bicarbonate buffering system of the ocean? When the ocean absorbs CO2, it removes the abundance of calcium carbonate importantly in the form of bio-available aragonite. This buffering system works really well at regulating the ocean's pH, but to a point. Once the buffer can no longer keep up, the saturation of calcium carbonate decreases; this prevents lower trophic-level invertebrates from calcifying. Not to mention the combined effects of temperature and CO2. And we don't really know how it will impact other species.
